value.summary: Organize accepted conditional consequences of the exactly encoded Gohari--Liu--Nair Theorem 9 premise, including private-message row expansion, auxiliary-receiver marginalization, the resulting receiver-infimum upper-bound formula, and finite-support local reductions.

value.title: Theorem 9 cited-premise private-message foundations
value.summary:
Assume the cited Gohari--Liu--Nair Theorem 9 outer-bound premise exactly as encoded in theorem9_spec.json and displayed for review in SOURCE_TRANSCRIPTION.md: for every finite auxiliary-receiver law T_{G,K|X,Y,Z}, achievable rates obey the stated factorization, equations (19a)-(19p), and both side conditions. Then setting R0=0 and exhaustively expanding the displayed minima and interval conditions gives exactly the independently generated local 30-row system; the exhaustive single-output term audit proves that replacing G,K by their input-only product marginals preserves the entire system, and hence for the physical BSSC C_sum <= inf_{finite-output binary-input T_{G|X},T_{K|X}} B(G,K). With the explicit extended-real local definitions (including sup(empty set)=-infinity), V_Q(G,K) <= V(1/2;G,K) <= B(G,K), and every Q0-supported row depends on the receiver channels only through (c,g,k,c), making V_0(g,k) finite and well defined on its realizable (g,k)-domain. No PDF-origin, source-fidelity, rendering, or visual-semantic assertion is part of this claim.

Scope qualifications:
- The result is conditional on the explicitly assumed Theorem 9 premise; it does not prove that theorem or authenticate its cited manuscript source.
- No PDF-origin, source-fidelity, rendering, or visual-semantic assertion is established.
- The capacity conclusion is an upper-bound formula, not an unconditional numerical evaluation of that infimum.
- The well-definedness and finiteness of V_0(g,k) apply on the realizable (g,k)-domain.

value.title: Proof of the conditional Theorem 9 private-message foundations
value.summary: Under the exact encoded Theorem 9 premise, the accepted proof sets R0=0, expands all minimum branches and both interval side conditions into 30 scalar rows, and compares them term by term with an independently generated L=3 path system using only the displayed chain-rule normalizations. An exhaustive audit shows that every output-bearing mutual-information term contains only one of Y, G, K, or Z, so replacing G and K by their input-only product marginals preserves every required marginal and every row. The proof then applies the specialized system at fixed q,G,K to obtain the stated receiver-infimum capacity upper-bound formula without interchanging optimization orders. Posterior identities expressed through J_A(t), together with J_A(0)=J_A(1)=0, establish the Q0 midpoint-value reduction; an explicit zero-rate hierarchy and individual-rate rows establish finiteness on the realizable domain. The argument proves only the accepted conditional claim and does not prove or authenticate the assumed Theorem 9 premise or numerically evaluate the receiver infimum.

value.title: Exact Theorem 9 specialization and single-output-term audit
value.summary: The supplied standard-library verifier reads the exact structured premise, expands its private-message branches and side conditions, independently constructs the L=3 path rows, normalizes only by I(U,W;A)=I(W;A)+I(U;A|W) and its V analogue, and compares all 30 rows exactly. It also checks the exhaustive 3/12/12/3 single-output term audit used in the product-marginal reduction. The tool establishes only the audited downstream specialization; it performs no PDF authentication, source-fidelity verification, numerical optimization, or proof of the assumed Theorem 9 premise.
